validated_work_order.approach: Derive the lower bound from the schedule's own recurrence instead of a constant. For a recurring schedule, the match window for occurrence D should be (previousOccurrence(D), D] - the day after the previous occurrence through D itself. That window is exactly as wide as the schedule's recurrence interval, so it covers an early payment of any size the reporter's scenario can produce, while remaining strictly narrower than the gap between two consecutive occurrences, so no single transaction can ever satisfy two occurrences. This answers both review objections at once: the window is not a constant that can be too small, and it cannot double-count. Validated by running it as a scratch vitest against the real Condition/rschedule pipeline: monthly occurrences produce disjoint windows and a transaction dated 2026-10-15 satisfies exactly one; a daily schedule produces start == occurrenceDate, i.e. no widening, which is precisely what the daily double-count objection requires. The previous occurrence is obtained with the same reverse rschedule lookup the codebase already uses in getNextDate, driven from the date condition's own start value. Keep the exact-date behaviour for auto-posted schedules (posts_transaction true), where the existing comment's reasoning still holds, and for one-time schedules, which have no recurrence to derive an interval from. Keep the existing 2-day fallback for schedules with no date condition at all. The helper stays the single seam, so all three callers get the fix together.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: The previous plan (v1) was rejected on three grounds: a constant 2-day lookback cannot cover the reporter's unbounded early payment; widening the window double-counts daily schedules in the forecast; and its AC-5 cited no test CI runs. I re-reproduced the bug with a 7-day gap (and a 31-day future-due variant), confirming objection 1 empirically, and derived a window from the schedule's own recurrence interval - (previousOccurrence, D] - which resolves objections 1 and 2 with one change: it is wide enough for any early payment and, because the window equals the gap between consecutive occurrences, the windows are disjoint by construction so one transaction can satisfy at most one occurrence. Measured: daily schedules get zero widening. Objection 3 is answered by naming two specific test cases by path, including a forecast-schedules.test.ts that does not exist yet. I also found that the prior plan's claim its existing tests encoded the bug is wrong - those are first-occurrence cases the fix leaves unchanged.

files.change: In getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate, replace the bare `return occurrenceDate` short-circuit for the `dateCond?.op === 'is'` branch with a recurrence-derived lower bound for recurring schedules: look up the occurrence immediately preceding `occurrenceDate` via the schedule's own date condition (same reverse rschedule lookup getNextDate already performs, driven from the date condition's `start` value) and return the day after it. Keep returning the exact occurrenceDate when `schedule.posts_transaction` is true, when the date condition is a fixed date rather than a recurrence, and when the date condition has no preceding occurrence (first occurrence of the series). Preserve the existing 2-day lookback fallback for schedules that carry no date condition at all.
files.why: This single helper defines the lower bound for all three callers (getHasTransactionsQuery in useSchedules and advanceSchedulesService, and isScheduleOccurrencePosted in forecast-schedules). A window derived from the recurrence is bounded by the schedule's own interval, which is the only bound that covers the reporter's unbounded early payment and simultaneously cannot let one transaction satisfy two occurrences - a constant of any size fails one of those two.

qa_script: 1. `yarn start`, open $PREVIEW_URL, click 'Try the demo' on the welcome screen. This creates a 'Phone bills' schedule: Dominion Power, Bank of America, monthly on the 2nd, date condition op 'is', posts_transaction false (created by packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:966-975).
2. Go to Schedules, right-click 'Phone bills', choose 'Post transaction'. Confirm the Schedules page shows 'Paid' and that the Bank of America register no longer shows the 'Phone bills' schedule row.
3. Open Bank of America. The posted transaction reads 10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Categorize | 120.00.

4. Click that transaction's date cell, navigate back one month, and pick a date SEVEN DAYS before the original due date (e.g. 09/25/2026). This is the reproduced gap: seven days early, well beyond the two days the rejected plan assumed.
5. THE BUG, before the fix: the schedule row reappears in the register as '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00' and the Schedules page flips from 'Paid' to 'Due'.

6. After the fix, step 4 must leave the register with only the posted transaction and no 'Phone bills' schedule row, and the Schedules page must still read 'Paid'. Reload the page and confirm it stays that way.

7. Future-due variant, the reporter's own shape: back on Schedules, right-click 'Phone bills' > 'Skip next scheduled date' so next_date moves to next month (a ~31-day gap). Post it, then re-date the posted transaction to today. The status must remain 'Paid' and no schedule row may reappear.

8. Regression sweep: on the Schedules page, 'Skip next scheduled date' and 'Post transaction today' must still behave as before; an auto-posted schedule (create one with 'Automatically add transaction' enabled) must still match on its exact date; and a forecast for an account with a re-dated scheduled transaction must not double-count the bill - confirm one daily recurring schedule paid once still projects its later occurrences.
residual_risks: ONE BOUNDARY NEEDS A DECISION BEFORE MERGE: a payment dated exactly ON the previous occurrence's date is ambiguous. With a half-open window (previousOccurrence, D], a payment on 2026-10-02 for a schedule due 2026-11-02 whose previous occurrence was 2026-10-02 does NOT satisfy the 11-02 occurrence, because it belongs to the 10-02 one. That is the conservative and self-consistent reading (each transaction satisfies at most one occurrence, which is what AC-5 requires), but the exact-boundary case stays broken. Closing the window on both ends would fix that case but let one transaction satisfy two adjacent occurrences - the exact double-count AC-5 forbids. The implementer should confirm this reading rather than silently widen the window. My reproduction of the reporter's 31-day variant lands on exactly this boundary, so it is not hypothetical.

Deriving the lower bound now requires an rschedule reverse lookup per schedule, where the current code is a constant-time branch. getHasTransactionsQuery maps over all schedules, so this runs for every schedule on every status refresh. The lookup is bounded (reverse, take 2) and rule objects are already built elsewhere in the same path, but it is a real change in cost profile and is the one thing I did not measure.

isScheduleOccurrencePosted (forecast-schedules.ts:207) reuses this helper and applies its own upper bound of occurrenceDate. With disjoint windows this is sound, but the forecast path currently has NO test file at all (no forecast-schedules test exists in packages/loot-core/src/server/forecast/), which is why the prior plan's 'run the suite' criterion proved nothing. The new forecast-schedules.test.ts is load-bearing, not optional.

The auto-post path in advanceSchedulesService reads the same status. Auto-posted schedules deliberately keep the exact-date bound, so their behaviour is unchanged - but if an implementer widens the window for posts_transaction schedules as well, a genuinely missed occurrence could be treated as paid and never auto-posted. The tests must keep the posts_transaction case on exact matching.

Widening the lower bound is a shared-behaviour change across three callers, one of which (advanceSchedulesService) writes to the database by advancing next_date. A window that is too wide could advance a recurring schedule past an occurrence that was never paid, permanently skipping a bill. The disjointness property is what makes this safe and must be asserted by a test, not assumed.

validated_work_order.root_cause: Whether a schedule occurrence counts as paid is derived from a date comparison around schedule.next_date rather than from the existence of a transaction linked to that schedule. getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate returns next_date itself as the lower bound whenever the schedule's date condition op is 'is' (packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:95-97), and getHasTransactionsQuery then selects only transactions with schedule = <id> AND date >= that bound (schedules.ts:165-193). Posting creates the transaction dated exactly next_date, so it matches and getStatus returns 'paid'. Editing the transaction's date to any earlier day moves it below the lower bound, the same query stops matching it, hasTrans goes false, getStatus falls back to comparing next_date with today and returns 'due' (schedules.ts:52-76), and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions regenerates the schedule row because 'due' is in the isForPreview list (schedules.ts:425-434). The transaction stays linked to the schedule the whole time; only the date comparison changed. The lower bound is the wrong shape for the problem: the gap between next_date and the real payment date is a property of how early the user paid, not a constant, and it is bounded above only by the schedule's own recurrence interval.

validated_work_order.understanding: Posting a scheduled transaction and then moving that transaction's date to an earlier day makes the schedule reappear as an un-posted row in the transactions table and flips its status back from 'Paid'. The prior plan for this issue was rejected because its fix (a constant 2-day lookback) cannot cover the reporter's scenario, and because widening the window double-counts daily schedules. I re-reproduced the bug with a 7-day gap and traced it to the same helper, and I validated a different fix shape that covers both objections. Root mechanism: a schedule occurrence is considered 'already paid' purely because a transaction linked to that schedule exists on or after the occurrence date, so any early payment - of any size - falls below the comparison and the occurrence reverts to unpaid. The link itself survives; only the date comparison changed, and nothing in the date-edit path repairs it. Reproduction, in the demo budget against http://localhost:3001: 'Phone bills' (Dominion Power, Bank of America, monthly on the 2nd, date condition op 'is', posts_transaction false) was posted from the Schedules page, which correctly removed its preview row and set the status to 'Paid'. Editing the posted transaction's date from 10/02/2026 to 09/25/2026 - seven days early - brought the row straight back, reading '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00', and the Schedules page flipped that schedule from 'Paid' to 'Due'. It survives a full page reload, so this is persisted state rather than a stale render. I also reproduced the reporter's future-due variant: skipping 'Phone bills' forward to 11/02/2026, posting it, and re-dating the transaction to today 10/02/2026 flipped the status from 'Paid' to 'Scheduled' - a 31-day gap. No console errors or page errors were emitted at any step.
